### NEWS RELEASE

April 19, 2018 

### Coalition for Renewable Natural Gas Releases New North American RNG Project Map and Database 

Number of Production Facilities Grows 85% in Past Four Years

SACRAMENTO, CA – The Coalition for Renewable Natural Gas (RNG Coalition) announced the release today of a new map and project database of renewable natural gas (RNG) production facilities in North America. The refreshed database reveals that there are now at least 76 operational RNG facilities in the U.S. and Canada, representing 85% growth from the 41 projects that were built between 1982 and 2014. 

“Redeeming our organic waste-streams by converting them to renewable natural gas for productive end-use epitomizes sustainability,” said RNG Coalition CEO Johannes Escudero. “Increased RNG development, deployment and use leads to greater adoption of the renewables we use to drive, heat and power our homes and businesses, while ensuring the reliability of our electric grid and decarbonizing our gas distribution systems.”

The RNG Coalition established a goal in 2015 to double the number of RNG production facilities in North America by 2025. There were 51 RNG facilities at the time. The new database shows that the North American RNG industry is on pace to reach the goal in half that time: an additional 23 RNG production facilities are currently under construction and another 25 have reached stages of substantial development prior to commencing construction. 

“Converting waste steams into RNG is a very clear success story, largely as a result of the Renewable Fuels Standard,” said Jay Hopper, Vice President of industry developer Aria Energy. “Since the environmental benefits of RNG were ruled eligible to generate D3 Renewable Identification Numbers in 2014, private capital has funded dozens of new projects all across the continent, and dozens more are in process.” 

The updated RNG facility database was derived through months of research on RNG facilities by the California-based RNG Coalition and by Energy Vision, a clean energy and renewable fuels nonprofit organization out of New York. The database and map are hosted on the RNG Coalition’s 【34†website†r20.rs6.net】 and will be updated as new production facilities are brought online.

ABOUT THE COALITION FOR RENEWABLE NATURAL GAS 

The RNG Coalition represents the renewable natural gas industry in North America, including companies that produce, or otherwise support production and distribution of biogas-derived renewable natural gas (RNG or biomethane) – a domestic, clean, low-carbon, and renewable source of power, heat and fuel that makes up the predominant share of cellulosic biofuel in North America. For more information, please see 【35†RNGCoalition.com†r20.rs6.net】.

[Image 2: Vision RNG’s Gas Project is Now Operational] 

Vision RNG’s Landfill Gas (LFG) to Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) project at Meridian Waste’s Eagle Ridge Landfill in Bowling Green Missouri is now operational. The project uses 1,500 scf/min of LFG and produces 375,000 MMBtu of RNG annually, enough renewable gas to heat approximately 8,800 homes per year. (Source: Business Wire)

Vision RNG’s Landfill Gas (LFG) to Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) project at Meridian Waste’s Eagle Ridge Landfill in Bowling Green Missouri is now operational. The project uses 1,500 scf/min of LFG and produces 375,000 MMBtu of RNG annually, enough renewable gas to heat approximately 8,800 homes per year.

“This is the first of several LFG to RNG projects VRNG will be bringing online, including projects in Kentucky, Alabama, South Carolina and Oklahoma,” Bill Johnson, CEO of VRNG, said in a press release.

The Missouri Clean Energy Project is the first of three projects that Meridian Waste has partnered with Vision RNG. RNG production is seen as a carbon-neutral energy solution that lowers methane emissions and reduces dependence while still utilizing current natural gas infrastructure.

“Our business is safely and judiciously managing solid waste collections and disposal so that it benefits the greater community while protecting the environment,” Gregg Asciutto, Missouri area president of Meridian Waste said. “By converting our landfill gas into pipeline quality clean energy, we manage potential odors more effectively, reduce greenhouse-gas emissions, and capture a once wasted renewable resource to fuel more efficient trucks and operations throughout the region.”

### Coalition for Renewable Natural Gas Releases New North American RNG Project Map and Database 

Number of Production Facilities Grows 85% in Past Four Years

SACRAMENTO, CA – The Coalition for Renewable Natural Gas (RNG Coalition) announced the release today of a new map and project database of renewable natural gas (RNG) production facilities in North America. The refreshed database reveals that there are now at least 76 operational RNG facilities in the U.S. and Canada, representing 85% growth from the 41 projects that were built between 1982 and 2014. 

“Redeeming our organic waste-streams by converting them to renewable natural gas for productive end-use epitomizes sustainability,” said RNG Coalition CEO Johannes Escudero. “Increased RNG development, deployment and use leads to greater adoption of the renewables we use to drive, heat and power our homes and businesses, while ensuring the reliability of our electric grid and decarbonizing our gas distribution systems.”

The RNG Coalition established a goal in 2015 to double the number of RNG production facilities in North America by 2025. There were 51 RNG facilities at the time. The new database shows that the North American RNG industry is on pace to reach the goal in half that time: an additional 23 RNG production facilities are currently under construction and another 25 have reached stages of substantial development prior to commencing construction. 

“Converting waste steams into RNG is a very clear success story, largely as a result of the Renewable Fuels Standard,” said Jay Hopper, Vice President of industry developer Aria Energy. “Since the environmental benefits of RNG were ruled eligible to generate D3 Renewable Identification Numbers in 2014, private capital has funded dozens of new projects all across the continent, and dozens more are in process.” 

The updated RNG facility database was derived through months of research on RNG facilities by the California-based RNG Coalition and by Energy Vision, a clean energy and renewable fuels nonprofit organization out of New York. The database and map are hosted on the RNG Coalition’s 【34†website†r20.rs6.net】 and will be updated as new production facilities are brought online.

ABOUT THE COALITION FOR RENEWABLE NATURAL GAS 

The RNG Coalition represents the renewable natural gas industry in North America, including companies that produce, or otherwise support production and distribution of biogas-derived renewable natural gas (RNG or biomethane) – a domestic, clean, low-carbon, and renewable source of power, heat and fuel that makes up the predominant share of cellulosic biofuel in North America. For more information, please see 【35†RNGCoalition.com†r20.rs6.net】.

#  Vision RNG’s Gas Project is Now Operational

The project is expected to provide heat to nearly 9,000 homes.

Hart Energy Staff

Thu, 08/10/2023 - 11:39 AM

[Image 2: Vision RNG’s Gas Project is Now Operational] 

Vision RNG’s Landfill Gas (LFG) to Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) project at Meridian Waste’s Eagle Ridge Landfill in Bowling Green Missouri is now operational. The project uses 1,500 scf/min of LFG and produces 375,000 MMBtu of RNG annually, enough renewable gas to heat approximately 8,800 homes per year. (Source: Business Wire)

Vision RNG’s Landfill Gas (LFG) to Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) project at Meridian Waste’s Eagle Ridge Landfill in Bowling Green Missouri is now operational. The project uses 1,500 scf/min of LFG and produces 375,000 MMBtu of RNG annually, enough renewable gas to heat approximately 8,800 homes per year.

“This is the first of several LFG to RNG projects VRNG will be bringing online, including projects in Kentucky, Alabama, South Carolina and Oklahoma,” Bill Johnson, CEO of VRNG, said in a press release.

The Missouri Clean Energy Project is the first of three projects that Meridian Waste has partnered with Vision RNG. RNG production is seen as a carbon-neutral energy solution that lowers methane emissions and reduces dependence while still utilizing current natural gas infrastructure.

“Our business is safely and judiciously managing solid waste collections and disposal so that it benefits the greater community while protecting the environment,” Gregg Asciutto, Missouri area president of Meridian Waste said. “By converting our landfill gas into pipeline quality clean energy, we manage potential odors more effectively, reduce greenhouse-gas emissions, and capture a once wasted renewable resource to fuel more efficient trucks and operations throughout the region.”

### NEWS RELEASE

April 19, 2018 

### Coalition for Renewable Natural Gas Releases New North American RNG Project Map and Database 

Number of Production Facilities Grows 85% in Past Four Years

SACRAMENTO, CA – The Coalition for Renewable Natural Gas (RNG Coalition) announced the release today of a new map and project database of renewable natural gas (RNG) production facilities in North America. The refreshed database reveals that there are now at least 76 operational RNG facilities in the U.S. and Canada, representing 85% growth from the 41 projects that were built between 1982 and 2014. 

“Redeeming our organic waste-streams by converting them to renewable natural gas for productive end-use epitomizes sustainability,” said RNG Coalition CEO Johannes Escudero. “Increased RNG development, deployment and use leads to greater adoption of the renewables we use to drive, heat and power our homes and businesses, while ensuring the reliability of our electric grid and decarbonizing our gas distribution systems.”

The RNG Coalition established a goal in 2015 to double the number of RNG production facilities in North America by 2025. There were 51 RNG facilities at the time. The new database shows that the North American RNG industry is on pace to reach the goal in half that time: an additional 23 RNG production facilities are currently under construction and another 25 have reached stages of substantial development prior to commencing construction. 

“Converting waste steams into RNG is a very clear success story, largely as a result of the Renewable Fuels Standard,” said Jay Hopper, Vice President of industry developer Aria Energy. “Since the environmental benefits of RNG were ruled eligible to generate D3 Renewable Identification Numbers in 2014, private capital has funded dozens of new projects all across the continent, and dozens more are in process.” 

The updated RNG facility database was derived through months of research on RNG facilities by the California-based RNG Coalition and by Energy Vision, a clean energy and renewable fuels nonprofit organization out of New York. The database and map are hosted on the RNG Coalition’s 【34†website†r20.rs6.net】 and will be updated as new production facilities are brought online.

ABOUT THE COALITION FOR RENEWABLE NATURAL GAS 

The RNG Coalition represents the renewable natural gas industry in North America, including companies that produce, or otherwise support production and distribution of biogas-derived renewable natural gas (RNG or biomethane) – a domestic, clean, low-carbon, and renewable source of power, heat and fuel that makes up the predominant share of cellulosic biofuel in North America. For more information, please see 【35†RNGCoalition.com†r20.rs6.net】.

#  Vision RNG’s Gas Project is Now Operational

The project is expected to provide heat to nearly 9,000 homes.

Hart Energy Staff

Thu, 08/10/2023 - 11:39 AM

[Image 2: Vision RNG’s Gas Project is Now Operational] 

Vision RNG’s Landfill Gas (LFG) to Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) project at Meridian Waste’s Eagle Ridge Landfill in Bowling Green Missouri is now operational. The project uses 1,500 scf/min of LFG and produces 375,000 MMBtu of RNG annually, enough renewable gas to heat approximately 8,800 homes per year. (Source: Business Wire)

Vision RNG’s Landfill Gas (LFG) to Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) project at Meridian Waste’s Eagle Ridge Landfill in Bowling Green Missouri is now operational. The project uses 1,500 scf/min of LFG and produces 375,000 MMBtu of RNG annually, enough renewable gas to heat approximately 8,800 homes per year.

“This is the first of several LFG to RNG projects VRNG will be bringing online, including projects in Kentucky, Alabama, South Carolina and Oklahoma,” Bill Johnson, CEO of VRNG, said in a press release.

The Missouri Clean Energy Project is the first of three projects that Meridian Waste has partnered with Vision RNG. RNG production is seen as a carbon-neutral energy solution that lowers methane emissions and reduces dependence while still utilizing current natural gas infrastructure.

“Our business is safely and judiciously managing solid waste collections and disposal so that it benefits the greater community while protecting the environment,” Gregg Asciutto, Missouri area president of Meridian Waste said. “By converting our landfill gas into pipeline quality clean energy, we manage potential odors more effectively, reduce greenhouse-gas emissions, and capture a once wasted renewable resource to fuel more efficient trucks and operations throughout the region.”

### NEWS RELEASE

April 19, 2018 

### Coalition for Renewable Natural Gas Releases New North American RNG Project Map and Database 

Number of Production Facilities Grows 85% in Past Four Years

SACRAMENTO, CA – The Coalition for Renewable Natural Gas (RNG Coalition) announced the release today of a new map and project database of renewable natural gas (RNG) production facilities in North America. The refreshed database reveals that there are now at least 76 operational RNG facilities in the U.S. and Canada, representing 85% growth from the 41 projects that were built between 1982 and 2014. 

“Redeeming our organic waste-streams by converting them to renewable natural gas for productive end-use epitomizes sustainability,” said RNG Coalition CEO Johannes Escudero. “Increased RNG development, deployment and use leads to greater adoption of the renewables we use to drive, heat and power our homes and businesses, while ensuring the reliability of our electric grid and decarbonizing our gas distribution systems.”

The RNG Coalition established a goal in 2015 to double the number of RNG production facilities in North America by 2025. There were 51 RNG facilities at the time. The new database shows that the North American RNG industry is on pace to reach the goal in half that time: an additional 23 RNG production facilities are currently under construction and another 25 have reached stages of substantial development prior to commencing construction. 

“Converting waste steams into RNG is a very clear success story, largely as a result of the Renewable Fuels Standard,” said Jay Hopper, Vice President of industry developer Aria Energy. “Since the environmental benefits of RNG were ruled eligible to generate D3 Renewable Identification Numbers in 2014, private capital has funded dozens of new projects all across the continent, and dozens more are in process.” 

The updated RNG facility database was derived through months of research on RNG facilities by the California-based RNG Coalition and by Energy Vision, a clean energy and renewable fuels nonprofit organization out of New York. The database and map are hosted on the RNG Coalition’s 【34†website†r20.rs6.net】 and will be updated as new production facilities are brought online.

ABOUT THE COALITION FOR RENEWABLE NATURAL GAS 

The RNG Coalition represents the renewable natural gas industry in North America, including companies that produce, or otherwise support production and distribution of biogas-derived renewable natural gas (RNG or biomethane) – a domestic, clean, low-carbon, and renewable source of power, heat and fuel that makes up the predominant share of cellulosic biofuel in North America. For more information, please see 【35†RNGCoalition.com†r20.rs6.net】.

#  Vision RNG’s Gas Project is Now Operational

The project is expected to provide heat to nearly 9,000 homes.

Hart Energy Staff

Thu, 08/10/2023 - 11:39 AM

[Image 2: Vision RNG’s Gas Project is Now Operational] 

Vision RNG’s Landfill Gas (LFG) to Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) project at Meridian Waste’s Eagle Ridge Landfill in Bowling Green Missouri is now operational. The project uses 1,500 scf/min of LFG and produces 375,000 MMBtu of RNG annually, enough renewable gas to heat approximately 8,800 homes per year. (Source: Business Wire)

Vision RNG’s Landfill Gas (LFG) to Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) project at Meridian Waste’s Eagle Ridge Landfill in Bowling Green Missouri is now operational. The project uses 1,500 scf/min of LFG and produces 375,000 MMBtu of RNG annually, enough renewable gas to heat approximately 8,800 homes per year.

“This is the first of several LFG to RNG projects VRNG will be bringing online, including projects in Kentucky, Alabama, South Carolina and Oklahoma,” Bill Johnson, CEO of VRNG, said in a press release.

The Missouri Clean Energy Project is the first of three projects that Meridian Waste has partnered with Vision RNG. RNG production is seen as a carbon-neutral energy solution that lowers methane emissions and reduces dependence while still utilizing current natural gas infrastructure.

### NEWS RELEASE

April 19, 2018 

### Coalition for Renewable Natural Gas Releases New North American RNG Project Map and Database 

Number of Production Facilities Grows 85% in Past Four Years

SACRAMENTO, CA – The Coalition for Renewable Natural Gas (RNG Coalition) announced the release today of a new map and project database of renewable natural gas (RNG) production facilities in North America. The refreshed database reveals that there are now at least 76 operational RNG facilities in the U.S. and Canada, representing 85% growth from the 41 projects that were built between 1982 and 2014. 

“Redeeming our organic waste-streams by converting them to renewable natural gas for productive end-use epitomizes sustainability,” said RNG Coalition CEO Johannes Escudero. “Increased RNG development, deployment and use leads to greater adoption of the renewables we use to drive, heat and power our homes and businesses, while ensuring the reliability of our electric grid and decarbonizing our gas distribution systems.”

The RNG Coalition established a goal in 2015 to double the number of RNG production facilities in North America by 2025. There were 51 RNG facilities at the time. The new database shows that the North American RNG industry is on pace to reach the goal in half that time: an additional 23 RNG production facilities are currently under construction and another 25 have reached stages of substantial development prior to commencing construction. 

“Converting waste steams into RNG is a very clear success story, largely as a result of the Renewable Fuels Standard,” said Jay Hopper, Vice President of industry developer Aria Energy. “Since the environmental benefits of RNG were ruled eligible to generate D3 Renewable Identification Numbers in 2014, private capital has funded dozens of new projects all across the continent, and dozens more are in process.” 

The updated RNG facility database was derived through months of research on RNG facilities by the California-based RNG Coalition and by Energy Vision, a clean energy and renewable fuels nonprofit organization out of New York. The database and map are hosted on the RNG Coalition’s 【34†website†r20.rs6.net】 and will be updated as new production facilities are brought online.

ABOUT THE COALITION FOR RENEWABLE NATURAL GAS 

The RNG Coalition represents the renewable natural gas industry in North America, including companies that produce, or otherwise support production and distribution of biogas-derived renewable natural gas (RNG or biomethane) – a domestic, clean, low-carbon, and renewable source of power, heat and fuel that makes up the predominant share of cellulosic biofuel in North America. For more information, please see 【35†RNGCoalition.com†r20.rs6.net】.

### NEWS RELEASE

April 19, 2018 

### Coalition for Renewable Natural Gas Releases New North American RNG Project Map and Database 

Number of Production Facilities Grows 85% in Past Four Years

SACRAMENTO, CA – The Coalition for Renewable Natural Gas (RNG Coalition) announced the release today of a new map and project database of renewable natural gas (RNG) production facilities in North America. The refreshed database reveals that there are now at least 76 operational RNG facilities in the U.S. and Canada, representing 85% growth from the 41 projects that were built between 1982 and 2014. 

“Redeeming our organic waste-streams by converting them to renewable natural gas for productive end-use epitomizes sustainability,” said RNG Coalition CEO Johannes Escudero. “Increased RNG development, deployment and use leads to greater adoption of the renewables we use to drive, heat and power our homes and businesses, while ensuring the reliability of our electric grid and decarbonizing our gas distribution systems.”

The RNG Coalition established a goal in 2015 to double the number of RNG production facilities in North America by 2025. There were 51 RNG facilities at the time. The new database shows that the North American RNG industry is on pace to reach the goal in half that time: an additional 23 RNG production facilities are currently under construction and another 25 have reached stages of substantial development prior to commencing construction. 

“Converting waste steams into RNG is a very clear success story, largely as a result of the Renewable Fuels Standard,” said Jay Hopper, Vice President of industry developer Aria Energy. “Since the environmental benefits of RNG were ruled eligible to generate D3 Renewable Identification Numbers in 2014, private capital has funded dozens of new projects all across the continent, and dozens more are in process.” 

The updated RNG facility database was derived through months of research on RNG facilities by the California-based RNG Coalition and by Energy Vision, a clean energy and renewable fuels nonprofit organization out of New York. The database and map are hosted on the RNG Coalition’s 【34†website†r20.rs6.net】 and will be updated as new production facilities are brought online.

ABOUT THE COALITION FOR RENEWABLE NATURAL GAS 

The RNG Coalition represents the renewable natural gas industry in North America, including companies that produce, or otherwise support production and distribution of biogas-derived renewable natural gas (RNG or biomethane) – a domestic, clean, low-carbon, and renewable source of power, heat and fuel that makes up the predominant share of cellulosic biofuel in North America. For more information, please see 【35†RNGCoalition.com†r20.rs6.net】.

#  Vision RNG’s Gas Project is Now Operational

The project is expected to provide heat to nearly 9,000 homes.

Hart Energy Staff

Thu, 08/10/2023 - 11:39 AM

[Image 2: Vision RNG’s Gas Project is Now Operational] 

Vision RNG’s Landfill Gas (LFG) to Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) project at Meridian Waste’s Eagle Ridge Landfill in Bowling Green Missouri is now operational. The project uses 1,500 scf/min of LFG and produces 375,000 MMBtu of RNG annually, enough renewable gas to heat approximately 8,800 homes per year. (Source: Business Wire)

Vision RNG’s Landfill Gas (LFG) to Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) project at Meridian Waste’s Eagle Ridge Landfill in Bowling Green Missouri is now operational. The project uses 1,500 scf/min of LFG and produces 375,000 MMBtu of RNG annually, enough renewable gas to heat approximately 8,800 homes per year.

“This is the first of several LFG to RNG projects VRNG will be bringing online, including projects in Kentucky, Alabama, South Carolina and Oklahoma,” Bill Johnson, CEO of VRNG, said in a press release.

The Missouri Clean Energy Project is the first of three projects that Meridian Waste has partnered with Vision RNG. RNG production is seen as a carbon-neutral energy solution that lowers methane emissions and reduces dependence while still utilizing current natural gas infrastructure.

“Our business is safely and judiciously managing solid waste collections and disposal so that it benefits the greater community while protecting the environment,” Gregg Asciutto, Missouri area president of Meridian Waste said. “By converting our landfill gas into pipeline quality clean energy, we manage potential odors more effectively, reduce greenhouse-gas emissions, and capture a once wasted renewable resource to fuel more efficient trucks and operations throughout the region.”

### NEWS RELEASE

April 19, 2018 

### Coalition for Renewable Natural Gas Releases New North American RNG Project Map and Database 

Number of Production Facilities Grows 85% in Past Four Years

SACRAMENTO, CA – The Coalition for Renewable Natural Gas (RNG Coalition) announced the release today of a new map and project database of renewable natural gas (RNG) production facilities in North America. The refreshed database reveals that there are now at least 76 operational RNG facilities in the U.S. and Canada, representing 85% growth from the 41 projects that were built between 1982 and 2014. 

“Redeeming our organic waste-streams by converting them to renewable natural gas for productive end-use epitomizes sustainability,” said RNG Coalition CEO Johannes Escudero. “Increased RNG development, deployment and use leads to greater adoption of the renewables we use to drive, heat and power our homes and businesses, while ensuring the reliability of our electric grid and decarbonizing our gas distribution systems.”

The RNG Coalition established a goal in 2015 to double the number of RNG production facilities in North America by 2025. There were 51 RNG facilities at the time. The new database shows that the North American RNG industry is on pace to reach the goal in half that time: an additional 23 RNG production facilities are currently under construction and another 25 have reached stages of substantial development prior to commencing construction. 

“Converting waste steams into RNG is a very clear success story, largely as a result of the Renewable Fuels Standard,” said Jay Hopper, Vice President of industry developer Aria Energy. “Since the environmental benefits of RNG were ruled eligible to generate D3 Renewable Identification Numbers in 2014, private capital has funded dozens of new projects all across the continent, and dozens more are in process.” 

The updated RNG facility database was derived through months of research on RNG facilities by the California-based RNG Coalition and by Energy Vision, a clean energy and renewable fuels nonprofit organization out of New York. The database and map are hosted on the RNG Coalition’s 【34†website†r20.rs6.net】 and will be updated as new production facilities are brought online.

ABOUT THE COALITION FOR RENEWABLE NATURAL GAS 

The RNG Coalition represents the renewable natural gas industry in North America, including companies that produce, or otherwise support production and distribution of biogas-derived renewable natural gas (RNG or biomethane) – a domestic, clean, low-carbon, and renewable source of power, heat and fuel that makes up the predominant share of cellulosic biofuel in North America. For more information, please see 【35†RNGCoalition.com†r20.rs6.net】.

### NEWS RELEASE

April 19, 2018 

### Coalition for Renewable Natural Gas Releases New North American RNG Project Map and Database 

Number of Production Facilities Grows 85% in Past Four Years

SACRAMENTO, CA – The Coalition for Renewable Natural Gas (RNG Coalition) announced the release today of a new map and project database of renewable natural gas (RNG) production facilities in North America. The refreshed database reveals that there are now at least 76 operational RNG facilities in the U.S. and Canada, representing 85% growth from the 41 projects that were built between 1982 and 2014. 

“Redeeming our organic waste-streams by converting them to renewable natural gas for productive end-use epitomizes sustainability,” said RNG Coalition CEO Johannes Escudero. “Increased RNG development, deployment and use leads to greater adoption of the renewables we use to drive, heat and power our homes and businesses, while ensuring the reliability of our electric grid and decarbonizing our gas distribution systems.”

The RNG Coalition established a goal in 2015 to double the number of RNG production facilities in North America by 2025. There were 51 RNG facilities at the time. The new database shows that the North American RNG industry is on pace to reach the goal in half that time: an additional 23 RNG production facilities are currently under construction and another 25 have reached stages of substantial development prior to commencing construction. 

“Converting waste steams into RNG is a very clear success story, largely as a result of the Renewable Fuels Standard,” said Jay Hopper, Vice President of industry developer Aria Energy. “Since the environmental benefits of RNG were ruled eligible to generate D3 Renewable Identification Numbers in 2014, private capital has funded dozens of new projects all across the continent, and dozens more are in process.” 

The updated RNG facility database was derived through months of research on RNG facilities by the California-based RNG Coalition and by Energy Vision, a clean energy and renewable fuels nonprofit organization out of New York. The database and map are hosted on the RNG Coalition’s 【34†website†r20.rs6.net】 and will be updated as new production facilities are brought online.

ABOUT THE COALITION FOR RENEWABLE NATURAL GAS 

The RNG Coalition represents the renewable natural gas industry in North America, including companies that produce, or otherwise support production and distribution of biogas-derived renewable natural gas (RNG or biomethane) – a domestic, clean, low-carbon, and renewable source of power, heat and fuel that makes up the predominant share of cellulosic biofuel in North America. For more information, please see 【35†RNGCoalition.com†r20.rs6.net】.

#  Vision RNG’s Gas Project is Now Operational

The project is expected to provide heat to nearly 9,000 homes.

Hart Energy Staff

Thu, 08/10/2023 - 11:39 AM

[Image 2: Vision RNG’s Gas Project is Now Operational] 

Vision RNG’s Landfill Gas (LFG) to Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) project at Meridian Waste’s Eagle Ridge Landfill in Bowling Green Missouri is now operational. The project uses 1,500 scf/min of LFG and produces 375,000 MMBtu of RNG annually, enough renewable gas to heat approximately 8,800 homes per year. (Source: Business Wire)

Vision RNG’s Landfill Gas (LFG) to Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) project at Meridian Waste’s Eagle Ridge Landfill in Bowling Green Missouri is now operational. The project uses 1,500 scf/min of LFG and produces 375,000 MMBtu of RNG annually, enough renewable gas to heat approximately 8,800 homes per year.

“This is the first of several LFG to RNG projects VRNG will be bringing online, including projects in Kentucky, Alabama, South Carolina and Oklahoma,” Bill Johnson, CEO of VRNG, said in a press release.

The Missouri Clean Energy Project is the first of three projects that Meridian Waste has partnered with Vision RNG. RNG production is seen as a carbon-neutral energy solution that lowers methane emissions and reduces dependence while still utilizing current natural gas infrastructure.

“Our business is safely and judiciously managing solid waste collections and disposal so that it benefits the greater community while protecting the environment,” Gregg Asciutto, Missouri area president of Meridian Waste said. “By converting our landfill gas into pipeline quality clean energy, we manage potential odors more effectively, reduce greenhouse-gas emissions, and capture a once wasted renewable resource to fuel more efficient trucks and operations throughout the region.”

### NEWS RELEASE

April 19, 2018 

### Coalition for Renewable Natural Gas Releases New North American RNG Project Map and Database 

Number of Production Facilities Grows 85% in Past Four Years

SACRAMENTO, CA – The Coalition for Renewable Natural Gas (RNG Coalition) announced the release today of a new map and project database of renewable natural gas (RNG) production facilities in North America. The refreshed database reveals that there are now at least 76 operational RNG facilities in the U.S. and Canada, representing 85% growth from the 41 projects that were built between 1982 and 2014. 

“Redeeming our organic waste-streams by converting them to renewable natural gas for productive end-use epitomizes sustainability,” said RNG Coalition CEO Johannes Escudero. “Increased RNG development, deployment and use leads to greater adoption of the renewables we use to drive, heat and power our homes and businesses, while ensuring the reliability of our electric grid and decarbonizing our gas distribution systems.”

The RNG Coalition established a goal in 2015 to double the number of RNG production facilities in North America by 2025. There were 51 RNG facilities at the time. The new database shows that the North American RNG industry is on pace to reach the goal in half that time: an additional 23 RNG production facilities are currently under construction and another 25 have reached stages of substantial development prior to commencing construction. 

“Converting waste steams into RNG is a very clear success story, largely as a result of the Renewable Fuels Standard,” said Jay Hopper, Vice President of industry developer Aria Energy. “Since the environmental benefits of RNG were ruled eligible to generate D3 Renewable Identification Numbers in 2014, private capital has funded dozens of new projects all across the continent, and dozens more are in process.” 

The updated RNG facility database was derived through months of research on RNG facilities by the California-based RNG Coalition and by Energy Vision, a clean energy and renewable fuels nonprofit organization out of New York. The database and map are hosted on the RNG Coalition’s 【34†website†r20.rs6.net】 and will be updated as new production facilities are brought online.

ABOUT THE COALITION FOR RENEWABLE NATURAL GAS 

The RNG Coalition represents the renewable natural gas industry in North America, including companies that produce, or otherwise support production and distribution of biogas-derived renewable natural gas (RNG or biomethane) – a domestic, clean, low-carbon, and renewable source of power, heat and fuel that makes up the predominant share of cellulosic biofuel in North America. For more information, please see 【35†RNGCoalition.com†r20.rs6.net】.

Wilmington Airport offers a range of parking options to its passengers, including short-term, long-term, hourly, premium, standard, economy, and other parking options. If you are traveling with a pet, you might find useful a specially designated area for the comfort of your traveling pet. The pet areas are located to the left and right of the airport entrance in the grass area. Please note that pets are not allowed inside the terminal, except for the service animals.

You can find two ATMs at the airport. The pre-security ATM is located behind the Information Desk and the post-security ATM is located to your right after entering. The terminal is operating 24/7.

## Wilmington International Airport Parking

Wilmington airport parking offers six options for you to choose from. The Hourly parking, Main Daily, North Daily, Premium Daily, Standard Daily, and Economy Daily (Long Term) lots. Not taking into account the Cell Phone Lot and a separate Employee parking lot, which greatly reduces travelers' parking load. The most convenient option is the Hourly lot, as it is located right in front of the terminal. The Main Daily lot is located right behind it and takes up to a few minutes to get there. North, Standard, and Premium Daily lots are located around the big main lot in the center. Wilmington Airport Long Term parking lot is located a little bit further, behind the Standard and Premium Daily lots. All the Wilmington NC Airport parking lots include handicap parking. Please note that no Wilmington Airport parking garage is available, all the lots are outdoor type only. If you are looking for a garage option with cleaning or vacuuming services included, you might consider searching for parking near Wilmington Airport. You can easily find all the parking information on our website.

## Wilmington NC Airport Parking Rates

Wilmington Airport parking rates start after the first free 30 minutes. The next 30 minutes (31-60 minutes) cost $1. Every additional hour is $1 each. Hourly parking lot maximum daily rate is $24. The Daily parking lot charges $10, North Daily lot - $12, and the Standard Daily lot - $10 per 24 hours. The cost of Long Term parking at Wilmington NC Airport is $8 per day.

PARKING OPTIONS   

Travelers have a variety of parking options at ILM. Please review the parking lot map, rates, and availability to plan ahead for the option that works best for you. 

Handicap parking is available in all of the public parking lots.  

All ILM parking lots are credit-debit only and accept payment by Visa, Mastercard or American Express. In all lots, you may park free for the first 30 minutes. If a technical difficulty or payment challenge arises, staff is onsite during commercial flight operations hours to assist customers as necessary and may be reached by calling 【38†910-341-4336†tel:9103414336】. (Curious to learn more about ILM’s future improvements? 【13†Learn more about our future plans to expand parking, improve the curb-front, and realign the roadways】.)

DRIVER INFO

If you are dropping off or picking up passengers from ILM, please continue straight on Airport Blvd. to the terminal. You may pick up/drop off your passenger at the curb but please do not leave your vehicle unattended. Parking at the curb of the terminal is strictly prohibited and will result in ticketing and/or towing by Airport police.

30 minutes of free parking are allowed in all lots, so feel free to park in the short term lot (the closest to the terminal) to pick up and drop off guests that may need assistance.

Additionally, if you are picking up passengers you may wait for them in the Cell Phone Lot. To access the lot, continue on Airport Blvd. past the main airport terminal. Turn right onto the first road, Trask Drive and continue straight after the stop sign. There will be signs directing you to the cell phone lot. Once the passenger has contacted you that they are ready for pickup, simply proceed to the front of the terminal building.

HANDICAP ASSISTANCE 

If you need special assistance between your parking space and the airport terminal, please make arrangements in advance of your travel date by calling 910-341-4336. Advance notice is highly recommended so the team may provide the best service possible. Further, for assistance to and from the gate area for your flight, you may make arrangements directly with your airline, when booking or managing your trip.

# Wilmington International Airport (ILM), Wilmington Parking

Who hasn’t been to the airport only to spend an eternity searching for a parking spot, and then get overcharged? Parking at airports is annoying but it doesn’t have to be.

Parking is invariably one of the most stressful and costly aspects of flying. By the time you find a space and park your car, you’re usually already running late.

No more aimlessly searching for a parking spot near Wilmington International Airport! This guide has all the info you need, including free and paid options, as well as covered and valet services. By the end of this article, you’ll be an expert on finding the right parking solution based on your needs.

## Best Parking at Wilmington International Airport, Wilmington

The Main Daily Parking is the best place to park at Wilmington International Airport. It’s close to the airport terminal, and it offers short-term and long-term parking. Parking at Main Daily Parking is $12 a day.

The address for Main Daily Parking is:

Airport Blvd, Wilmington, NC 28405, United States.

The lot is equipped with security cameras, so you can feel safe leaving your car there.

The Main Daily Parking parking area has an automated pay station that accepts cash and credit cards. You can also purchase a prepaid parking permit online or at the airport for discounted rates.

## Free Parking at Wilmington International Airport

This tip is for all of the budget-savvy travelers out there: did you know that there is free parking at Wilmington International Airport? I was ecstatic when I found out, and now I always make sure to take advantage of this perk!

Does Wilmington International Airport have free parking? Wilmington International Airport has free parking located at 3609 Tristram Pl, Wilmington, NC 28403, United States.

## Wilmington International Airport Long Term Parking

Wilmington International Airport offers both short and long term parking options to those traveling. The airport is open 24/7, all year round, so you can always park no matter the time of day or night. Long term parking at Wilmington International Airport is $24 a day .

The address for long term parking at Wilmington International Airport is:

Airport Blvd, Wilmington, NC 28405, United States.

For more information on Wilmington International Airport long-term parking, please visit the airport website or contact the airport directly.

## Cheapest Parking Near Wilmington International Airport

If cost is your top priority for Wilmington International Airport parking, look no further.

The cheapest parking at Economy is the uncovered lot, which is $8 a day .

The address for the cheapest parking at Wilmington International Airport is:

Tradewinds Dr, Wrightsboro, NC 28405, United States

There are a few key things to consider if you want to get the best deal on airport parking.

The first consideration is location. You can find airport parking both on and off the airport property. Off-site parking may require a shuttle bus to get to the terminal, but it often cheaper.

You’ll want to compare long-term and short-term rates when deciding how to park, but keep in mind that you may need to take a shuttle if your parking duration extends beyond the limit for cheap rates.

Lastly, make sure to compare rates for different airports. Some have loyalty programs which give discounts to people who fly frequently, so it’s definitely worth looking into if you want to save some money.

## Covered Parking at ILM Airport

Covered parking is a great way to keep your car protected from the weather. Not only does it keep your car clean and dry, but it also keeps it from getting too hot or too cold.

Does Wilmington International Airport have covered parking?

Wilmington International Airport has covered parking. It is located in the short-term parking lot. Covered parking at Wilmington International Airport is $24 a day.

Covered parking is a great way to avoid any potential damage that may come from hail or snow.

Here is the address for covered parking at Wilmington International Airport:

Airport Blvd, Wilmington, NC 28405, United States

## Valet Parking at Wilmington Airport

Does Wilmington International Airport have valet parking?

Yes, Wilmington International Airport offers valet parking. There is a designated area for valet parking just outside the terminal building. The cost for valet parking is $20 a day.

Valet parking at Wilmington International Airport is at:

Airport Blvd, Wilmington, NC 28405, United States

Parking at the airport doesn’t have to be a pain. With this handy guide, you can find the perfect spot near Wilmington International Airport, whether you’re looking for free or paid options, covered or valet services.

# Wilmington Airport Parking

[Image 4: Wilmington Airport Parking ILM Logo] 

ILM

Wilmington International Airport (ILM) is a public airport located just a few miles north of Wilmington, North Carolina, New Hanover County. Wilmington International is providing flights to eight destinations: Atlanta (ATL), Boston (BOS), Charlotte (CLT), Chicago O'Hare (ORD), Dallas Fort Worth (DFW), New York City (LGA), Philadelphia (PHL), Washington DC (DCA) and Washington Dulles (IAD). The airport operates more than 1 million passengers and around 3 million lbs. of cargo annually.

Wilmington Airport terminal provides all the necessary services. The design of the terminal covers food and beverages available for both pre- and post-security areas, as well as gift shops and news kiosks. Free Wi-Fi is a complimentary gift for all the ILM’s guests. To start, simply use the “Fly ILM” network.

If you are traveling with a pet, you might find useful a specially designated area for the comfort of your traveling pet. The pet areas are located to the left and right of the airport entrance in the grass area. Please note that pets are not allowed inside the terminal, except for the service animals.

You can find two ATMs at the airport. The pre-security ATM is located behind the Information Desk and the post-security ATM is located to your right after entering. The terminal is operating 24/7.

## Wilmington International Airport Parking

Wilmington airport parking offers six options for you to choose from. The Hourly parking, Main Daily, North Daily, Premium Daily, Standard Daily, and Economy Daily (Long Term) lots. Not taking into account the Cell Phone Lot and a separate Employee parking lot, which greatly reduces travelers' parking load. The most convenient option is the Hourly lot, as it is located right in front of the terminal. The Main Daily lot is located right behind it and takes up to a few minutes to get there. North, Standard, and Premium Daily lots are located around the big main lot in the center. Wilmington Airport Long Term parking lot is located a little bit further, behind the Standard and Premium Daily lots. All the Wilmington NC Airport parking lots include handicap parking. Please note that no Wilmington Airport parking garage is available, all the lots are outdoor type only. If you are looking for a garage option with cleaning or vacuuming services included, you might consider searching for parking near Wilmington Airport. You can easily find all the parking information on our website.

## Wilmington NC Airport Parking Rates

Wilmington Airport parking rates start after the first free 30 minutes. The next 30 minutes (31-60 minutes) cost $1. Every additional hour is $1 each. Hourly parking lot maximum daily rate is $24. The Daily parking lot charges $10, North Daily lot - $12, and the Standard Daily lot - $10 per 24 hours. The cost of Long Term parking at Wilmington NC Airport is $8 per day.

This allows travelers to simply drive their own car to the off-site lot and then relax on the shuttle ride, rather than having to find alternate transportation to the airport. Many off-site parking companies also have self-serve check-ins, allowing customers to bypass waiting in line to park.

Off-site airport parking lots typically have more parking spaces available than on-site parking lots. This makes it easier to find an open spot, especially during peak travel seasons. Travelers don’t have to worry about circling endlessly looking for parking at the airport.

### 3. Secure

Most off-site airport parking facilities provide heightened security measures to keep vehicles safe. Safety features often include 24/7 video surveillance, security patrols, gated entrances, and individual space alarm systems.

Off-site airport parking is typically safe and secure, giving travelers peace of mind while they are traveling. Travelers can feel assured knowing their vehicle is protected while they are away.

### 4. Additional Services

In addition to parking and shuttle services, many off-site parking companies offer extra amenities and conveniences for travelers. These can include:

  * Covered or garage parking options to protect vehicles from weather elements

  * Car wash and detail services so vehicles are cleaned upon return
  * Oil changes and vehicle maintenance while parked
  * Valet parking for added convenience

  * 24/7 customer service help if needed
  * Luggage assistance on the shuttle

The extra services and amenities provided enhance the travel experience for flyers.

### Benefits for Different Types of Travelers

Off-site airport parking caters to all types of travelers and trips:

#### Vacation Travelers

For those going on vacation, off-site parking can mean significant cost savings on parking fees. This allows extra money to spend on the getaway itself. Off-site parking facilities allow easy access to luggage assistance on the shuttle for those with lots of bags.

#### Business Travelers

Road warriors can take advantage of off-site parking’s flexibility for long-term parking. Additional amenities like car washes and maintenance checks keep vehicles in top shape in between trips.

#### Families

Families benefit from more spacious parking for large vehicles like vans and SUVs. Covered parking protects vehicles with car seats and strollers inside. Shuttle services mean less walking for families.

#### Travelers with Disabilities

Those with disabilities can benefit from off-site parking’s close parking spaces and shuttle services which minimize walking. Some facilities also offer wheelchair assistance.

## How to Choose an Off-Site Airport Parking Facility

When selecting an off-site airport parking provider, travelers should consider the following factors:

### 1. Location and Proximity to the Airport

The ideal off-site parking facility has a location close to the airport, usually within 5 miles or less. Proximity to the airport ensures shuttle rides are short and convenient. Longer shuttle rides can mean more time in transit.

### 2. Security Measures in Place

Examine the security protocols the off-site parking company has in place, such as surveillance systems, security staff, and gate access. Companies that prioritize security can provide greater peace of mind.

### 3. Price Comparison

Travelers should compare rates across multiple off-site parking providers. Some companies offer discounts for booking in advance or for longer-term parking. Make sure to factor in any fees or surcharges as well.

### 4. Availability of Shuttle Service

The timing and frequency of the shuttle service to the airport is key. Shuttles should operate continuously so travelers don’t miss flights. Shared ride shuttles are common, so be sure to allow enough time.

### 5. Customer Reviews and Ratings

Reading customer feedback provides insight into service quality, facilities, and overall satisfaction from past travelers. High ratings indicate a reputable parking provider.

### 6. Extra Services Offered

Consider which on-site amenities are priorities, like covered parking, car washes, or valet service. Compare options across providers.

### 7. Booking Process

The reservation process should be quick and straightforward online or by phone. Clear booking policies and prompt email confirmations are favorable.

### 8. Payment Options

Most off-site parking companies accept major credit cards and some accept debit cards or PayPal. Understand payment terms and when you will be charged.

### 9. Cancellation Policy

Check if reservations can be canceled or changed. Many companies provide flexibility to modify or cancel bookings, sometimes with a fee.

### 10. Operating Hours

Off-site parking facilities should be open early and close late to accommodate flight schedules. Facilities open 24/7 provide maximum flexibility.

## Why Choose Off-Site Airport Parking?

There are many reasons travelers may opt for off-site over on-site airport parking:

  * Business travelers who take frequent, longer trips can maximize savings with off-site parking.

  * Families traveling together can get more spacious parking spots for large vehicles.
  * Those with early morning or late night flights benefit from facilities open 24/7.
  * Travelers with disabilities can benefit from shuttle service and closer parking spots.

Off-site airport parking companies are generally well-rated by customers based on factors like affordable rates, security, convenience, and customer service. Reviews indicate most travelers have positive experiences using off-site airport parking.

The off-site airport parking industry is rapidly expanding to meet traveler demand:

  * The off-site airport parking market is expected to grow to $20 billion by 2027, according to Allied Market Research.

  * New off-site parking facilities are opening near major airports each year.
  * Parking companies are enhancing amenities to attract travelers.

Off-site airport parking provides an affordable, convenient alternative to airport parking. Here is more on the top parking providers, how to book off-site parking, tips for using these facilities, common misconceptions, and how it compares to on-site parking.

## Top 5 Off-Site Airport Parking Companies in the US

The off-site airport parking industry has expanded rapidly across the US. Here are 5 of the top national off-site parking providers:

### 1. Park ‘N Fly

Founded in 1967, Park ‘N Fly operates near over 60 airports nationwide. The company prides itself on excellent customer service and amenities like covered garages, valet parking, car washes, pet boarding, and electric vehicle charging stations. Park ‘N Fly has a user-friendly website and mobile app for reserving parking spots. They frequently offer discounts and rewards programs for travelers.

### 2. The Parking Spot

With 75 locations across 23 states, The Parking Spot is one of the largest near-airport parking companies. They focus on premium services like covered garages, complimentary car washes, and bottled water upon return. The Parking Spot also offers valet parking, electric car charging, pet services, and luggage assistance. Customers give high marks for their friendly shuttle drivers.

### 3. Park Shuttle & Fly

Park Shuttle & Fly provides off-site parking with complimentary shuttles at over 20 major airports coast-to-coast. They offer both outdoor and covered garage parking with security patrols. Unique amenities include air conditioning, power outlets, and Wi-Fi on shuttles. There are many positive reviews for Park Shuttle & Fly’s affordable rates and attentive customer service.

### 4. Smart Park

Known for spacious parking lots, Smart Park has locations at 13 busy airports. They offer uncovered and covered parking with video monitoring, along with maintenance and car wash services. Smart Park has flexible cancellation policies and accommodates larger vehicles. Customers highlight their prompt shuttle service, clean facilities, and friendly staff. 

### 5. Peachy Airport Parking

A top parking provider in the South, Peachy Airport Parking operates near major hubs like Atlanta, Nashville, Orlando, and Tampa. Their amenities include covered parking, car charging stations, and a rewards program. Peachy Airport Parking is lauded for low rates, cleanliness, security features, and responsive customer service agents. 

## How to Book an Off-Site Airport Parking Spot

Booking off-site airport parking is simple, with most companies offering online reservations or phone booking:

### Online Reservations

The easiest way to book off-site parking is through the company’s website. After selecting your airport:

  * Choose your dates of travel and confirm availability.

  * Select covered or uncovered parking if offered. 
  * Indicate if you need any extra services like car wash or maintenance.
  * Provide contact and payment details to complete reservation.

  * You’ll receive a confirmation email with arrival instructions.

### Phone Reservations

To reserve parking over the phone:

  * Call the company and specify your airport location and travel dates.

  * Request covered or uncovered parking if available.
  * Ask about add-ons like valet or maintenance if desired.
  * Provide contact information and payment details.

  * Obtain your confirmation number and arrival instructions.

Some companies offer mobile apps for added convenience booking and managing reservations. Most also provide airport-specific driving directions right to the facility.

## Tips for Using Off-Site Airport Parking Facilities

To ensure a smooth experience using off-site airport parking:

The 【10†promise is significant】. But companies and scientists have been tinkering with the technology for over a decade without any commercial deployment. As a solar material, perovskites are fickle—they’re sensitive to water, heat, and light. And some researchers warn time may be running out. 

“I have a feeling that if in the next two to three years there’s no perovskite products, the market may decrease its confidence in this technology,” says Bin Chen, a research assistant professor who focuses on perovskite technology at Northwestern University. 

Researchers and startups including Swift are working feverishly to develop those products, emboldened by recent progress on making perovskites more durable. In recent months, some of the world’s largest solar companies have also given the technology votes of confidence, by investing in pilot manufacturing lines or purchasing perovskite startups. 

Now these companies must prove they can overcome the 【11†struggles that have bedeviled perovskites for years】, while producing millions of panels that perform with record-breaking efficiency. 

### ‘On the back’ of silicon

The key to success for perovskites, many of these companies believe, will be integrating them with proven solar technologies, which could lend perovskites some of their stability and their hard-earned market confidence. 

## Related Story

【9†Super-efficient solar cells: 10 Breakthrough Technologies 2024】

Solar cells that combine traditional silicon with cutting-edge perovskites could push the efficiency of solar panels to new heights.

“The main entry point for perovskites to the market is literally on the back of silicon,” says Barry Rand, a professor of electrical and computer engineering at Princeton University. 

Today, more than 90% of solar panels sold worldwide are made from crystalline silicon. Decades of experience with that technology mean developers know how to plan projects around it, and financiers know how to price investments for projects that use it. 

Layering perovskites onto these panels could give solar companies an edge in a highly competitive industry. “If you can crack it—make a better solar module—you will make money out of it,” says Jenny Chase, a solar analyst at the research service BloombergNEF. “The idea is to make something that’s cheaper to manufacture per watt, and then you can sell it at a premium because it will be quite high efficiency.” 

That’s easier said than done. Perovskites, which are composed of metal halides and share a unique crystal structure, face two big challenges: increasing durability and scaling up production. Perovskites can react with oxygen in the air, or degrade when exposed to light—a pretty big problem for a solar product. 

To make perovskite tandems with more stable structures, companies plan to layer perovskites on other solar cells, using evaporation, printing (like ink on a newspaper), and even “spin-coating,” a technique that looks like spin art from the ‘90s. Changing the composition of the perovskite layer could also help them last longer. 

Chen and Rand are collaborators on two newly funded efforts, backed by 【12†millions of dollars from the US Department of Energy†www.highergov.com】, to test perovskite-silicon configurations that could be more durable and quicker to commercialize. Other participants include universities, several perovskite startups (including Swift), and the US National Renewable Energy Laboratory.  

### Staying power

Rand, whose team at Princeton studies how to stop perovskites from degrading, says the field has come a long way in the last seven years. Today's panels are better encapsulated to keep out water. Now he says it’s simply a game of elimination—determining which chemical components in a cell are most likely to react, and swapping them out. But he doesn’t think that further experimentation should hold back commercialization. 

“The results are, I think, promising enough to make those investments,” he says. “But it shouldn’t be thought about as [a] ‘job done.’ There’s still many breakthroughs, mainly with respect to stability, to still emerge.”

## Related Story

【13†10 Breakthrough Technologies 2024】

Every year, we look for promising technologies poised to have a real impact on the world. Here are the advances that we think matter most right now.

Tomas Leijtens, a cofounder and the chief technology officer of Swift, says the company can now expose its cells to temperatures up to 70 °C while operating them in light without degradation. “That was something that was, I would say, unthinkable five years ago,” he says, seated at a table ornamented with a hot-pink perovskite model. 

But the industry must ensure that every cell will be that durable; worldwide, companies manufacture hundreds of millions of solar panels every year, each containing dozens of cells. Before they’re used in projects, panels must pass rigorous industry tests, like enduring quick temperature changes, humidity, and hail. Swift, which was founded in 2017, hasn’t started independent tests yet; for now it’s subjecting its cells to some of those conditions in its own lab and has one panel wired up on its roof. 

Startups like Swift and Oxford PV—a UK company spun out of a university research lab where some Swift founders once worked—are working alongside the industry’s largest companies to get tandems to market. Oxford PV says it will start shipping perovskite tandem panels to customers later this year. In May, Arizona-based First Solar, the largest solar manufacturer in the US, bought a European perovskite company called Evolar. 

In a release on its Evolar acquisition, First Solar CEO Mark Widmar said the company believes “high-efficiency tandem PV modules will define the future.” Just a few days later, Korea-based Hanwha Q Cells, another top manufacturer, said it was investing $100 million to set up a perovskite tandem pilot line. In 2022, Q Cells helped start Pepperoni, a European collaboration to advance tandems.  

[Image 1: closeup on a worker in a clean suit loading a tandem cell into a holder]Oxford PV plans to start shipping their tandem solar cells this year.

DAVID MALCOM/OXFORD PV

Researchers working on perovskites say commercial tandem cells could be years, not decades, away. Jean says Swift hopes to have a product ready to commercialize within four years. Incentives in the Inflation Reduction Act, which included credits for US-made clean energy products, should help. 

But perovskites have skeptics as well as supporters. Chase says today’s silicon panels are already good enough to help the world transition to clean energy and fight climate change. She has long questioned perovskites’ ability to upend the solar industry’s status quo.“You cannot make a semiconductor tech with momentum,” she says. “You need the tech to work.” 

Given how much solar energy will be needed to decarbonize the grid, however, perovskite backers say every bit of added efficiency will be important. 

“While it’s true that silicon is great, tandems are better,” says Leijtens. “In the fight to tackle climate change, we need to accelerate, not just say, ‘Oh, this is good enough—we’re done.’ Everything can continue to be improved.”

If the aquaculture operation were based in **Bermuda**, the regulatory landscape would change significantly, as Bermuda operates under its own jurisdiction. Here's an overview of how this might work:

### 1. **Bermuda's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ)**:
   - Bermuda has an EEZ that extends 200 nautical miles from its coast, similar to other countries. Any aquaculture operations within Bermuda's EEZ would fall under the jurisdiction of Bermuda's government and its local environmental and maritime laws.
   - The **Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR)** would likely oversee any aquaculture operations, including permitting, environmental regulations, and monitoring.

### 2. **Permitting Requirements in Bermuda**:
   - Bermuda has strict environmental policies, especially considering its marine biodiversity and reliance on the ocean for tourism and fisheries. You would need to obtain permits related to:
     - **Marine resources management**: To ensure that the operation does not negatively impact local ecosystems.
     - **Environmental Impact Assessments (EIA)**: Likely required to evaluate the environmental effects of the operation.
     - **Water quality and waste management**: Bermuda would regulate how fish farms handle waste, feed, and effluent, similar to the U.S.
   
### 3. **Operational Benefits in Bermuda**:
   - Bermuda's location in the Atlantic provides warm waters, which may be beneficial for certain species of fish.
   - Being under Bermudian jurisdiction could allow for less regulatory complexity compared to U.S. federal waters, depending on the scope and size of the operation. Bermuda is known to be interested in sustainable development and may be open to well-managed aquaculture initiatives.

### 4. **Bermuda's Legal and Environmental Framework**:
   - Bermuda's environmental policies are designed to protect marine ecosystems, and there would likely be **marine spatial planning** efforts in place to balance aquaculture with tourism, shipping, and other ocean uses.
   - The **Bermuda Government** has been exploring sustainable economic growth avenues, which could include aquaculture if aligned with their environmental goals.

To farm **salmon offshore**, assuming the fry are purchased at a size suitable for transfer to the open water pens, you would need the following basic equipment:

### 1. **Offshore Pens or Cages**:
   - **Submersible or Semi-Submersible Cages**: These cages are designed to withstand open-ocean conditions, including strong currents and waves. They are typically large, circular or square pens made from durable, corrosion-resistant materials like high-density polyethylene (HDPE). These cages allow for good water flow and oxygen exchange while containing the fish.
   - **Mooring Systems**: To anchor the cages securely to the ocean floor, robust mooring systems are necessary. These include anchors, buoys, and tension cables to keep the pens stable in varying ocean conditions.

### 2. **Feeding Systems**:
   - **Automated Feeders**: Offshore salmon farming typically uses automated feeding systems. These can be floating barges or systems that distribute feed pellets at regular intervals based on a programmed schedule or real-time monitoring of fish feeding behavior.
   - **Feed Storage**: Feed storage units on-site, typically on barges, hold the large quantities of pellets needed for the growing salmon. These systems are often paired with the automated feeding units.

### 3. **Monitoring and Control Systems**:
   - **Fish Monitoring Systems**: Underwater cameras and sensors are critical for monitoring fish health, behavior, and feeding. These systems help ensure fish are growing properly and reduce waste by adjusting feeding schedules based on real-time conditions.
   - **Water Quality Sensors**: Water quality is key for salmon health, so monitoring dissolved oxygen levels, temperature, salinity, and other water quality parameters is essential. This equipment ensures the water remains within optimal ranges for salmon growth.
   - **Biometric Sensors**: Some advanced systems can also monitor fish size and health, tracking growth rates and detecting any issues such as disease.

### 4. **Support Vessels**:
   - **Service Boats**: Regular maintenance of offshore pens, feeding systems, and fish health checks require boats capable of transporting personnel, equipment, and feed to and from the offshore site.
   - **Work Platforms or Barges**: Floating platforms or barges equipped with cranes and storage units are often used to store feed and equipment offshore. These barges may also house generators for power supply.

### 5. **Net Maintenance Systems**:
   - **Net Cleaning Equipment**: Biofouling (growth of algae, barnacles, etc.) on the nets is a common issue in offshore pens, so regular cleaning is necessary. This can be done using ROVs (remotely operated vehicles) equipped with brushes or scrapers, or divers performing manual cleaning.
   - **Predator Exclusion Nets**: To protect the salmon from predators like seals or sharks, additional predator nets may be used around the main pens.

### 6. **Harvesting Equipment**:
   - **Fish Pumps or Harvesting Cranes**: For harvesting mature salmon, fish pumps or cranes with nets are often used to remove fish from the pens and transfer them to boats for transportation to processing facilities.

### 7. **Power Supply**:
   - **Generators or Solar Power**: Since offshore locations may not have access to grid power, generators or renewable energy sources like solar panels are used to power the feeding systems, monitoring equipment, and communication tools.

### 8. **Support Infrastructure**:
   - **Processing Facilities (if nearby)**: Some operations may include or have access to nearby facilities for processing the harvested salmon. If this is not on-site, transportation to processing centers is required.

### 9. **Permitting and Environmental Monitoring Systems**:
   - **Environmental Monitoring Systems**: Compliance with environmental regulations requires continuous monitoring of the surrounding marine environment to ensure that the operation does not negatively impact local ecosystems. This involves monitoring waste output, benthic (seafloor) conditions, and the impact on nearby marine life.

Would you like to explore more about costs or specific case studies of successful offshore salmon farms?

You're right that flounder are bottom dwellers, which makes farming them in offshore pens more complex than species that swim in the water column. However, offshore pens for flounder are designed to accommodate their behavior by using specially designed mesh cages with flat bottoms that mimic the ocean floor. These pens allow the flounder to settle naturally, while being in a controlled environment that ensures water quality, oxygen levels, and food delivery. The pens are placed in locations with stable currents to provide clean water and reduce waste buildup.

In Belize, there are various options for purchasing private coastal land suitable for aquaculture, including areas with favorable water conditions for both shrimp and tilapia farming.

3. **Gales Point**:
   - Gales Point is another favorable location for aquaculture, offering **123 acres of seafront and lagoon-front land** for **$3 million**. This large tract offers a mix of access to both marine and freshwater, which is optimal for polyculture systems【74†source】.

4. **Turneffe Atoll**:
   - Properties on the atoll, such as an **8.83-acre lot** priced at **$250,000**, offer access to pristine waters, ideal for shrimp farming and sustainable aquaculture【76†source】.

### **Land Characteristics**:
   - These coastal properties generally provide access to both seawater and fresh/brackish water, essential for polyculture farming.
   - Placencia and Turneffe Atoll stand out for aquaculture due to their developed infrastructure, tourist presence, and access to export routes.

### **Cost**:
   - Prices for seafront and lagoon-front lots vary, from **$50,000 to $3 million** depending on the size, location, and access to infrastructure. Placencia and Gales Point are more expensive but offer proximity to established logistics and markets【75†source】【78†source】.

These areas offer great potential for aquaculture development with different price points and access to water suitable for polyculture operations. Would you like more details on any specific property or location?

metadata.text:
Access Points: Reach your secluded oasis by sea or through an 8-mile-long trail conveniently located off the coastal highway. Embrace the journey to your waterfront haven and savor the anticipation of the breathtaking views that await.  

Mountain Majesty: The property takes shape in an L-shaped configuration, with a stunning mountain range at the back, peaking at around 42 meters (138 feet). Explore the natural beauty and potential for elevated viewpoints and tranquil retreats amidst the mountains.  

Ben Loman Cave: Embark on a unique adventure halfway up the mountain to the "Ben Loman Cave," aptly named after the guides' cautionary phrase, "Bend Low Man." This private cave adds an element of mystery and exclusivity to the property, making it a standout feature for nature enthusiasts and explorers.  

Proximity to Amenities: La Democracia Village and the renowned Belize Zoo are approximately 9 miles away on the George Price Highway, providing a balance of tranquility and accessibility to amenities.  

Versatile Land Use: With a sprawling 72 acres, the possibilities are vast – from agricultural pursuits to tourism ventures, taking advantage of the one-of-a-kind private cave as a focal point for unique experiences.  

Don't miss the opportunity to own this rare gem in Belize!  

Connect with Hatem, your International REALTOR® at RE/MAX 1st Choice Belize, today to discuss this property's potential as your personal paradise, a profitable investment, or the first step to a new life in a stunning destination.

Access Points: Reach your secluded oasis by sea or through an 8-mile-long trail conveniently located off the coastal highway. Embrace the journey to your waterfront haven and savor the anticipation of the breathtaking views that await.  

Mountain Majesty: The property takes shape in an L-shaped configuration, with a stunning mountain range at the back, peaking at around 42 meters (138 feet). Explore the natural beauty and potential for elevated viewpoints and tranquil retreats amidst the mountains.  

Ben Loman Cave: Embark on a unique adventure halfway up the mountain to the "Ben Loman Cave," aptly named after the guides' cautionary phrase, "Bend Low Man." This private cave adds an element of mystery and exclusivity to the property, making it a standout feature for nature enthusiasts and explorers.  

Proximity to Amenities: La Democracia Village and the renowned Belize Zoo are approximately 9 miles away on the George Price Highway, providing a balance of tranquility and accessibility to amenities.  

Versatile Land Use: With a sprawling 72 acres, the possibilities are vast – from agricultural pursuits to tourism ventures, taking advantage of the one-of-a-kind private cave as a focal point for unique experiences.  

Don't miss the opportunity to own this rare gem in Belize!  

Connect with Hatem, your International REALTOR® at RE/MAX 1st Choice Belize, today to discuss this property's potential as your personal paradise, a profitable investment, or the first step to a new life in a stunning destination.
